title: Fitness & Nutrition Coaching
tagline: Train bodies safely, plan nutrition that works, coach in Dubai's heat and build a personal training business.

superpower.name: Pro Coach
superpower.description: Plans training and meals like a professional: better wellbeing, and more from fitness jobs.

syllabus: Week 1: How the body adapts: training principles and safe technique
Week 2: Nutrition: energy, protein and real-life meal plans
Week 3: Coaching people: assessment, motivation and training in the heat
Week 4: The business of personal training in Dubai

weeks.title: How the Body Adapts
weeks.objective: Use progressive overload, the right reps and good form to get results without injury.

slides.title: Progressive Overload and the Rep Ranges
slides.body: Muscles and fitness improve only when the body is asked to do a little more than last time, then given time to recover. That gradual increase is progressive overload: more weight, more reps, more sets, or better form and control.
bullets: Strength: heavy sets of about 1 to 5 reps
Muscle growth (hypertrophy): about 6 to 12 reps, close to failure
Muscular endurance: 15 reps or more
Recovery is when you actually improve: 48 hours or so before training the same muscles hard again
slides.example:
A beginner's squat over 4 weeks:
• Week 1: 3 sets of 10 at 40 kg
• Week 2: 3 × 12 at 40 kg (more reps)
• Week 3: 3 × 10 at 45 kg (more weight)
• Week 4: 4 × 10 at 45 kg (more sets)
Each week asks a little more, so the body keeps adapting.
slides.takeaway: Do a little more over time, recover well, repeat: that is the whole secret.

slides.title: Technique and Safety First
slides.body: A coach's first job is to keep clients safe. Every session starts with a warm-up, and every lift is taught with a neutral spine, controlled tempo and a full but comfortable range of motion.
bullets: Warm up 5 to 10 minutes: light cardio and movements that rehearse the workout
Brace the core and keep the spine neutral on squats, deadlifts and rows
Stop at sharp pain, dizziness or chest pain, and refer to a doctor
Screen clients with a health questionnaire (PAR-Q) before training
slides.takeaway: Results come from consistency, and consistency comes from never getting hurt.

lab.title: Programme Design Lab
lab.brief: Write a 4-week, 3-days-a-week full-body programme for a beginner, showing how the load progresses each week.
lab.deliverable: A table of exercises, sets, reps and load for each week.
lab.proTip: Simple programmes done consistently beat clever programmes done twice.

caseStudy.scenario: A new client wants to deadlift 100 kg in their first session to impress friends. They've never lifted before. What do you do?

options.explanation: Maximal lifts with no technique are a classic way to injure a beginner's back.

options.text: Teach the hip hinge with a light bar, build technique, and progress the weight over weeks.
options.explanation: Technique first, then load: safe, and it builds faster progress.

options.text: Refuse to teach deadlifts at all.
options.explanation: Deadlifts are valuable; they just need teaching properly.

quiz.question: Which rep range mainly builds muscle size?
quiz.explanation: Roughly 6 to 12 reps close to failure is the classic hypertrophy range.

quiz.question: What is progressive overload?
options: Gradually asking the body to do more over time
quiz.explanation: Gradually increasing the demand is what drives adaptation.

weeks.title: Nutrition That Works
weeks.objective: Work out energy needs, set protein targets and build meal plans people can stick to.

slides.title: Energy Balance: BMR and TDEE
slides.body: Body weight follows energy balance over time. Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR) is what the body burns at rest; Total Daily Energy Expenditure (TDEE) adds activity. Eat below TDEE to lose fat, above it to gain.
bullets: Mifflin-St Jeor: men 10 × weight (kg) + 6.25 × height (cm) − 5 × age + 5; women the same but − 161
Multiply by activity: about 1.2 (desk job) to 1.725 (very active)
A deficit of about 500 kcal a day loses roughly 0.5 kg a week
slides.example:
A 30-year-old man, 80 kg, 180 cm, training 3 to 5 times a week:
BMR = 10 × 80 + 6.25 × 180 − 5 × 30 + 5 = 800 + 1,125 − 150 + 5 = 1,780 kcal
TDEE = 1,780 × 1.55 ≈ 2,760 kcal
For fat loss: about 2,260 kcal a day.
slides.takeaway: Weight change is maths over time; the coaching is making it livable.

slides.title: Protein, Plates and Real Life
slides.body: Protein builds and repairs muscle and keeps people full. Most training clients do well on about 1.6 to 2.2 g of protein per kg of body weight. Then build meals simply, from food they actually like, including local favourites.
bullets: The plate method: half vegetables, a quarter protein, a quarter carbs, a thumb of fat
Good protein: chicken, fish (hammour, salmon), eggs, laban and Greek yogurt, lentils, chickpeas
Hydration: in Dubai's heat, often 2.5 to 3.5 litres a day or more, with electrolytes after heavy sweating
Fasting in Ramadan: train after iftar, and spread protein between iftar and suhoor
slides.takeaway: The best diet is the one your client can follow on a busy Tuesday.

lab.title: Meal Plan Lab
lab.brief: Calculate a client's TDEE and protein target, then write a one-day meal plan that hits both with food from Dubai supermarkets.
lab.deliverable: Calculations, a meal plan with calories and protein per meal, and a shopping list.
lab.proTip: Swap, don't ban: a lighter version of their favourite food beats a list of forbidden food.

caseStudy.scenario: A client has lost no weight in 4 weeks and swears they 'eat clean'. What's the best next step?

options.text: Cut their calories in half immediately.
options.explanation: Extreme cuts backfire: they're hard to stick to and lose muscle.

options.text: Ask them to log everything they eat and drink for a week, including drinks and snacks, then adjust.
options.explanation: Most stalls come from untracked calories: juices, coffee drinks, oils and weekend meals.

options.text: Tell them their metabolism is broken.
options.explanation: That isn't true and it destroys motivation.

quiz.question: What's a typical protein target for someone training?
quiz.explanation: About 1.6 to 2.2 g/kg supports muscle growth and repair.

quiz.question: A daily deficit of about 500 kcal loses roughly:
quiz.explanation: 500 × 7 = 3,500 kcal, roughly 0.5 kg of body fat.

weeks.title: Coaching People
weeks.objective: Assess clients, keep them motivated and train safely in extreme heat.

slides.title: Assessment and Goals
slides.body: Every programme starts with knowing the person: their health, history, schedule and real goal. Turn vague wishes into SMART goals: Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound.
bullets: Health questionnaire (PAR-Q) and, if needed, a doctor's clearance
Baseline: weight, waist measurement, photos, a push-up and plank test
From 'get fit' to 'lose 5 cm from my waist and do 10 push-ups in 12 weeks'
Review every 4 weeks and celebrate progress
slides.takeaway: What gets measured gets improved, and what gets celebrated gets repeated.

slides.title: Training in Dubai's Heat
slides.body: Summer in Dubai regularly passes 40°C with high humidity. Heat illness is a real danger for outdoor sessions, so coaches plan around it.
bullets: Train outdoors early morning or after sunset in summer, or move indoors
Signs of heat exhaustion: heavy sweating, dizziness, nausea, cramps: stop, cool down, rehydrate
Heat stroke is an emergency: confusion, hot dry skin, collapse. Call 998 for an ambulance and cool them immediately
Plan water breaks every 15 to 20 minutes
slides.takeaway: In the heat, the session plan bends to the weather, never the other way round.

lab.title: Client Onboarding Lab
lab.brief: Run a full onboarding for a friend: questionnaire, baseline tests, SMART goal and first-month plan.
lab.deliverable: The completed forms, baseline numbers and a 4-week plan.
lab.proTip: Clients stay for the relationship: remember their names, wins and struggles.

caseStudy.scenario: It's 41°C at 4pm and your client wants their usual outdoor beach bootcamp. What do you do?

options.text: Go ahead but tell them to drink water.
options.explanation: Peak afternoon heat is when heat illness is most likely.

options.text: Move the session indoors or to after sunset, and explain why.
options.explanation: Changing the time or place keeps them safe and keeps the habit going.
They lose the session and don't learn why.

quiz.question: What does SMART stand for?
quiz.explanation: SMART goals are specific, measurable, achievable, relevant and time-bound.

quiz.question: What number do you call for an ambulance in the UAE?
quiz.explanation: 998 is the ambulance; 999 is police and 997 is fire.

weeks.title: The Personal Training Business
weeks.objective: Register, price, find clients and keep them.

slides.title: Getting Qualified and Registered
slides.body: In the UAE, gyms usually require trainers to hold a recognised qualification and to be registered with REPs UAE (the Register of Exercise Professionals), plus first aid and CPR. Working freelance also needs the right licence or permit.
bullets: A recognised personal training qualification
REPs UAE registration, renewed yearly
First aid and CPR certificate
A freelance permit or trade licence if you work for yourself
slides.takeaway: Credentials open gym doors and give clients trust.

slides.title: Pricing and Keeping Clients
slides.body: Personal training is sold by the session or in packages. Packages bring commitment and steady income; results and relationships bring referrals.
bullets: Price from your costs, hours and the market
Packages: 10 or 20 sessions at a small discount, paid up front
Track results and share them (with permission)
Ask happy clients for referrals
slides.example:
Planning a month's income:
• 1 session: AED 300. A 10-session package: AED 2,700 (10% off).
• 12 clients doing 2 sessions a week = 96 sessions a month.
• At about AED 270 a session: AED 25,920 a month, before gym fees and costs.
slides.takeaway: Your best marketing is a client who got results and tells their friends.

lab.title: Business Plan Lab
lab.brief: Write a one-page plan for your training business: who you serve, prices, packages and how you'll find your first 10 clients.
lab.deliverable: A one-page plan with prices and a 30-day client plan.
lab.proTip: Niche down: 'strength for busy mums' wins more clients than 'fitness for everyone'.

caseStudy.scenario: Your client cancels sessions at the last minute every week. What's the professional fix?

options.text: Agree a clear 24-hour cancellation policy in writing at the start, and apply it kindly.
options.explanation: Clear terms agreed upfront protect your time and stay fair.

quiz.question: What is REPs UAE?
quiz.explanation: REPs UAE registers qualified exercise professionals.

quiz.question: Why sell session packages?
options: Commitment from clients and steadier income
quiz.explanation: Packages give clients commitment and you steady income.

questions.question: What drives fitness gains over time?
questions.explanation: Gradually more demand, with recovery, drives adaptation.

questions.question: BMR is:
questions.explanation: Basal Metabolic Rate is energy used at rest.

questions.question: TDEE adds what to BMR?
questions.explanation: Total Daily Energy Expenditure includes activity.

questions.question: A sign of heat stroke is:
questions.explanation: Confusion and hot, dry skin mean heat stroke: an emergency.

questions.explanation: Avoid the heat of the day.
